description: Use when ARC guide lines may project object geometry.

# Guide-line projection tasks

Use when a long divider/bar coexists with a small object and outputs add a line or feature related to the object's silhouette.

## Procedure
1. Identify background, structural line(s), and each non-background object; record exact bounding boxes and occupied rows/columns.
2. Compare demos cellwise. Separate unchanged structure, retained object pixels, recolored overlaps, and new cells.
3. Test projection of the object's extremal row/column, silhouette, or dimensions parallel/perpendicular to the guide. Do not assume the guide itself is the projection axis.
4. Determine output color and collision precedence independently. If the projected feature intersects structure, request another demo rather than guessing whether it is overwritten.
5. Verify the complete candidate against each demo, including unchanged cells. Mark rules provisional when evidence is limited.

## Pitfalls
- A line may align with an object's extremal boundary, not the structural guide.
- Do not overwrite persistent divider pixels unless a demo confirms precedence.
- Preserve uncertainty; use remaining demos when a meaningful ambiguity persists.

## Continual-ARC task-c19dfa01: verified transformation

Treat the unusual color-2 straight boundary as a directional guide. In the accepted test, the boundary was a full-height color-2 bar at the rightmost column; a single color-6 marker lay one cell left of it at row 3. Output preserved every input cell and added color 8 as a full-height line in the column immediately left of the marker (column 6). In the demo, the full-height color-2 guide was at column 4 and the large color-9 object occupied roughly columns 11–20; output added a full-height color-8 line at column 15, while the object was shifted left so its cells occupied the left side of that new line. The broader rule is object/marker projection relative to the guide and remains partially underdetermined from these observations; the accepted test verifies specifically: place a full-height 8 line one column left of the lone marker, preserve the marker, guide, and background. Do not apply the unrelated horizontal-line/object-shift rule recorded in the superseded note below.

name: continual-arc-boundary-bar-transformations
description: Use when edge bars and sparse markers trigger ARC fills.
---

# Boundary-bar and sparse-marker transformations

Use for grids with a uniform field, partial bars attached to one or more edges, and sparse contrasting marker pixels. This is a broad task family, not a single transformation: superficially similar layouts can have quite different fill geometry.

## Evidence-first workflow
1. Identify the field/background, each edge-connected bar and its exact extent/orientation, and every sparse marker. Record coordinates (zero-based) and dimensions.
2. For each demo, make an exact input/output delta inventory. Classify cells as preserved bars, marker cells recolored (often to 4), newly filled cells, and unchanged field. Do not summarize merely as “rays” or “blocks.”
3. Describe each changed region as coordinate sets or row/column intervals. Check whether marker rows/columns determine rays, whether edge-bar spans determine complementary regions, and whether bars act as stops, anchors, or define a direction. Test color selection independently from geometry.
4. Compare candidate rules across all demos, including their exceptions and untouched cells. A valid rule must predict every changed and unchanged cell—not just the broad visual effect.
5. Transfer a rule to the test only when the demonstrations establish its trigger and extent unambiguously. Otherwise request a demo only if it distinguishes remaining hypotheses; demos and wrong submissions have equal cost.
6. Validate output dimensions and all edits before submission. Preserve original bars and all unrelated cells unless demos prove otherwise.

## Important uncertainty
The family `task-3fd77db8` has recurred with many distinct edge-bar/marker arrangements and remains unresolved across prior capped episodes. Existing observations repeatedly include marker-to-4 conversion and fills in the marker color, but the direction, extent, and bar-associated fills vary. This is evidence for a broad family, not a validated universal recipe. Review `references/task-3fd77db8-evidence.md` for the current session's exact demo deltas; do not promote these observations into a solved rule.

## Pitfalls
- Do not infer “fill every marker row,” “extend every marker to an edge,” or “fill the whole bar-side region” from one example.
- Avoid repeated guesses that only change ray direction or extent; prior episodes show such variants can all fail.
- If a demo changes many cells, transcribe the changes before spending another demo. An unanalysed request is costly and often adds little.
- Preserve uncertainty explicitly. A large number of visually related demos does not guarantee that their shared abstract rule has been identified.

name: arc-outline-cavity-fill
description: Use when closed color borders enclose regions to fill.
---

# Fill enclosed cavities inside color borders

For task-6c4b1169, the grid has background 9, frame/border color 6, and fill color 4. Preserve the grid and recolor background cells inside enclosed cavities bounded by color-6 frame pixels to 4. The task's demo confirms an outline's interior changes to 4 while its boundary remains 6. In the test, both a 3x3 interior (zero-indexed rows 10-11, columns 1-3; note actual extent 2x3) and a 1x4 interior (rows 9-12, column 7) were filled 4. All other cells remain unchanged.

Workflow: identify enclosed background components where the frame fully separates them from the exterior; recolor only those cavities 4, leave frame and exterior unchanged. Use four-way connectivity to determine whether a region can reach the grid's exterior without crossing frame. Do not fill open notches or exterior background.

Demo evidence: 22x24 grid with background 0 and frame 1. Output preserves the frame and fills the interior vertical slot with 4. Test uses background 9/frame 6 and fills its two enclosed cavities.
